title: Queues: Fair, Ordered Processing
lead: A queue is a line where the first person in is the first person served. Unlike a stack, you add to the back and remove from the front — First In, First Out (FIFO).

sections.heading: Enqueue and Dequeue
sections.body: Enqueue adds to the back; dequeue removes from the front. Both are O(1). Queues model any system where order and fairness matter: print jobs, customer service, CPU task scheduling.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.body: A deque (double-ended queue) lets you add or remove from both ends. A priority queue always serves the highest-priority item first regardless of arrival order — used in Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm.

tryThis: Simulate a ticket counter: enqueue five names. Then serve (dequeue) them one by one and write the order. Confirm it matches the order they arrived.
